In `buildStaleAvailabilityGateStatus`, checking `summary.stale_8_row_gate_used === false` and `summary.small_subset_gate_used === false` can lead to incorrect status resolution if these properties are missing or undefined in the `summary` object. If they are missing, the conditions will evaluate to `false`, causing the status to default to `'unknown'` instead of `'rejected'`.

To ensure a robust, fail-closed design where stale gates are rejected by default when unspecified, use inequality checks (`!== true`) instead of strict equality to `false`.

```suggestion
function buildStaleAvailabilityGateStatus(summary) {
  const staleMinimalTrustedRejected = summary.stale_8_row_gate_used !== true
    || summary.source_map_stale_8_row_runtime_boundary_rejected === true;
  const servedEligibleRejected = summary.small_subset_gate_used !== true
    || summary.source_map_stale_small_subset_boundary_rejected === true
    || summary.stale_small_served_subset_boundary_rejected === true;
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

In `getFullBetaPostureRowByQuestionKey`, when falling back to searching `readModel.rows`, accessing `row.question_key` directly is unsafe if `readModel.rows` contains `null` or `undefined` values (which can happen with custom or mock read models in tests). This would result in a `TypeError`.

Using optional chaining (`row?.question_key`) provides a nullish-safe property access and prevents potential runtime crashes.

```suggestion
  return asArray(readModel.rows).find((row) => row?.question_key === normalizedQuestionKey) ?? null;
```
Fixed in 3c56d7dc4: fallback row lookup now uses null-safe `row?.question_key`, with regression coverage for null and undefined row entries.
Fixed in 3c56d7dc4: stale gate status now uses fail-closed `!== true` checks, with regression coverage for omitted summary flags.
